text:
Sam L: Quick questionI changed from full-time to part-time in March, stayed on HDHP, then back to full-time in August and switched plans to the non-HDHP. Can I still make the full-year HSA contribution or do we prorate? Also saw my 401k company match for June posted in September after the payroll vendor migrationhow should I reconcile pay-period attribution?

Priya (People Ops): Hi SamHSA eligibility: we use the last-month rule (Dec 1) or month-by-month counting to determine your max. If you were HSA-eligible on Dec 1 you can elect the full-year amount; otherwise it's pro-rated by eligible months. We have a simple worksheet to run both scenarios. For the 401k match timing, Marco can explain vendor migration quirks.

Marco (Payroll): Heyduring the vendor cutover we had an overlap window and a couple of match entries were deferred to the next payroll cycle; we can create a retro allocation in our records so the match is attributed to the original pay period for reporting, but the cash movement stays on the date it posted. If you want the match reflected on a specific pay period in your internal reconciliation, open a payroll ticket with the gross/net pay period ID and cc Priya. We need employee consent to re-attribute.

Sam L: If the match posts in a later pay period, could it push me over any deferral or overall contribution limits? I'm 49 so no catch-up yet, but want to avoid excess.

Jenna Benefits: Company match is employer contribution and doesn't count toward your elective deferral limit, but it does count toward the overall annual addition limit (IRC 415). For HSAif you choose the last-month rule but later lose eligibility in the next 12 months, you'd need to withdraw excess contributions or pay taxes/penalties. We can run numbers and recommend either electing last-month or pro-rating monthly.

Sam L: Great. What's the process to elect last-month rule or do a pro-rated HSA election midyear? Any forms?

Priya (People Ops): There's a one-page HSA eligibility election/last-month rule form and a short consent form for payroll retro allocations. I'll DM both forms and a link to the HSA worksheet. Fill the HSA form and indicate whether you want the last-month rule or pro-rated calculation. If you pick last-month and it's later invalidated, Benefits will work with you on corrective steps.

Marco (Payroll): Once you submit the payroll retro consent + the pay period ID, we can submit the adjustment request to the vendor. Lead time is ~10 business days for processing. Note: retro adjustments may show in a separate off-cycle entry.

HR-Bot: FYI: 2026 HSA limits are $3,850 individual / $7,750 family; HSA catch-up (50+) = $1,000. See benefits.redwood.com/limits. :link:

Sam L: Thanks folksPriya please send the worksheets. I'll sign and open a ticket with Marco. Appreciate the clarity. :thumbsup:
